summary: Family foundry (120 staff, EUR 19.3 M) in distress: half the shop floor idle, two shifts on short hours, bank watching monthly, owner seeking a successor. We are 6.7 % of its turnover, so we matter. HN 65-250 sells at cost, HN 100-315 below cost (70110 co-sources 40 %, 70190 qualified for HN 65-250). It historically gave way (kept 7 % of asks). Trade faster payment and volume for price; do not cut its margin hard.
notes: Needs cash (asked 10-day payment in two e-mails, two quotes and a call) and volume to fill idle capacity. Fears bank pressure and margin loss: 'cannot sign anything that lowers our margin'. Says it drops small accounts, but we are 6.7 % of its turnover. Succession adds continuity risk.
fears: losing volume while shop floor is idle

evidence.quote: the bank is watching every month. 'I cannot sign anything that lowers our margin now.'
two shifts are on short hours, and the MD spoke mostly about cash and the banks.

levers: binding volume to fill idle capacity
arguments: faster payment worth more than the price step to it
binding volume / forecast fills idle shifts
delivery record: OTD fell 92 % to 82 % vs 95 % target
second sources: 70110 active on HN 100-315, 70190 qualified on HN 65-250
avoid: demanding a straight margin cut ('cannot sign anything that lowers our margin')
changing terms after its final offer
threatening to leave while it is distressed (supply risk for us)
tactics: Offer 10-14 day payment early and ask for price in return: cash is its real need.
Add binding volume or extra HN 100-315 quota to fill its idle capacity.
Frame concessions as cash and volume, not as a lower margin.
Keep the opening moderate; prices sit at or below its own cost.
Watch supply continuity (succession, bank): prefer a stable deal over the last euro.
playbook.expected_concession: No arena data; history shows it gives way easily (kept 7 % of its asks), but distress caps how far price can fall without payment or volume trades.
